findings.title: Embedded-post author link color changed from 30% to 70% lightness in light themes
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` the color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original value as the first (light-theme) argument and uses the complement (100 - X) as the dark-theme argument. Here the light-theme argument was changed from 30% to 70%, so on default/light color schemes the bolded author username link becomes a very pale grey on a light background (much lower contrast than before). The intent was presumably `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Group member `.name` light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; it is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The first argument of `dark-light-choose` is the light-theme value, so this silently lightens the member name in light themes and makes it identical to the adjacent `.title` (which was intentionally lighter at 50%), losing the visual hierarchy between name and title. The light value should stay at 30% with a 70% dark complement.

findings.title: Mobile group member `.name` light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Since the first argument is the light-theme value, the member name becomes lighter than before on default themes and is now indistinguishable from the sibling `.title` (intentionally 50%). Keep 30% for light and use 70% for the dark branch.

findings.title: `.custom-message-length` light-theme color flipped from 70% to 30% lightness
findings.body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`; the new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The arguments look swapped relative to the rest of the PR (and relative to `desktop/modal.scss`, which uses 70%/30% for the same selector): light themes now get a much darker hint text than before, and the two platforms no longer match. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map `h3` light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme argument was changed from 20% to 50%, so the topic-map heading becomes noticeably lighter/lower contrast on default themes, and it no longer matches the desktop rule which correctly uses `dark-light-choose(... 20%, ... 80%)`. Light value should remain 20% with an 80% dark complement.

findings.title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification still uses raw scale-color($primary)
findings.body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` while every other `$primary` lightness usage in this file was converted to `dark-light-choose(...)`. On dark color schemes `$primary` is light, so lightening it by 50% yields an almost-white badge count instead of the intended muted tone, leaving this element inconsistent with the rest of the dark-theme work in this PR.

findings.title: `#file-uploading` color uses $secondary for both themes and is invisible on light themes
findings.body: Directly above the converted `#draft-status` rule, `#file-uploading { color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%); }` is left untouched. Because `$secondary` is the background color, in light themes this is a near-white text color on a light background, making the "uploading" status effectively invisible. Since this PR is specifically about making these muted colors theme-aware, this should become `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` like the neighbouring rule.
